title: Tissue Paper Flowers
summary: Fold soft tissue paper into fluffy flowers on pipe cleaner stems. A gentle first craft for little hands.
adultHelp: An adult can cut the tissue squares for children under 6.
safetyNotes: Pipe cleaner ends can poke. Fold the cut ends over, or have an adult do it.
Tissue paper and small scraps are not for mouths. Keep scraps away from children under 3.

materials.item: 8 squares of tissue paper, about 4 inches (10 cm), in 2 or 3 colors
A small cup or jar to display the flowers

steps.title: Stack the squares
steps.text: Lay the 8 tissue squares on top of each other. Line up the edges so the pile is neat.

steps.title: Fold like a fan
steps.text: Fold the pile back and forth in strips about the width of your thumb. Press each fold flat.

steps.title: Add the stem
steps.text: Pinch the middle of the folded strip. Wrap a pipe cleaner around the pinch and twist it tight.

steps.title: Fluff the petals
steps.text: Gently pull each layer up toward the middle, one at a time, until the flower is round and full.

steps.title: Show it off
steps.text: Stand your flower in a cup. Make a few more in different colors to make a bouquet.

tips: Round the ends of the folded strip with scissors for rounder petals.
heroAlt: Three fluffy tissue paper flowers in pink, yellow and blue on green pipe cleaner stems, standing in a small cup.
videoNarration: Stack your eight tissue squares and line up the edges.
Fold the stack back and forth like a fan, pressing each fold flat.
Pinch the middle and twist a pipe cleaner tightly around it.
Pull each layer up toward the middle to make the petals.
Put your flower in a cup and make some friends for it.
